name: developer-det (the Developer screen: reached with the developer mode on, its three panes, the local server started, its address copied, stopped, a start refused for a taken port, the server settings opened and CORS switched, a port that is not one, a port another program holds, the warning of a server on the local network without a token, the window of the tokens with one created, shown once and revoked, the model picker, the cards of the loaded models and of the exposed agents and workflows, an eject, the documentation read from its tree with its breadcrumb, previous and next, copy and the public site, a diagram left as code, the HTTP reference read from its overview to the page of a group, without a copy and with the public site, the link back to the settings, the logs read, filtered, cleared, folded and detached)
notes: Code-verified against routes/Developer.svelte, components/developer/DeveloperColumn.svelte, ServerBar.svelte, LoadModelButton.svelte, ServerSettingsPanel.svelte, ServerSettingRow.svelte, ServerTokensDialog.svelte, LocalServerPane.svelte, DocumentationPane.svelte, LogsPane.svelte, ServerModelsSection.svelte, ExposedItemsSection.svelte, SupportedEndpoints.svelte, ExamplesMenu.svelte, components/ai/LoadedModelCard.svelte, and components/developer/localServer.ts, serverSettings.ts, serverTokens.ts, servedItems.ts and examples.ts.

The start and the stop are real: they reach the compatible server of the runtime of the seeded home, on the port of its [server] section (7772 unless the seed says otherwise). A machine where another program holds that port shows the taken-port error on the first start and reds the steps that wait for the address; that is the machine, not the product.

The taken-port state is stubbed: start_local_server rejects with the LocalServerRefusal of crates/apollia-desktop/src/commands/local_server.rs (kind port_in_use). A field renamed there drifts here silently. The stub is cleared before the next start, which is real and clears the error.
The copy button is clicked, not asserted: the clipboard of the webview may refuse a write that no user gesture started, and the copy itself is held by the Vitest suite.
The picker of Load a model is opened and closed without choosing: the models of the seed are placeholders, and the loading window is played by llm-det.

The cards are stubbed: list_loaded_models resolves a LoadedModelsResponse (ui/src/lib/types/llm.ts), list_mcp_exposable a list of McpExposableItem (crates/apollia-desktop/src/commands/mcp_bridge.rs), get_workflow a WorkflowView (ui/src/lib/ipc/workflows.ts), unload_loaded_model an UnloadedModel. A field renamed there drifts here silently. The seed loads no model and exposes nothing the book could count on. The stubs are armed while the documentation view is shown, so the local server pane reads them when it mounts again; they are all cleared after the eject.
The foot Supported endpoints is asserted, not clicked: while the documentation pane reads no page it opens the documentation site in the browser of the machine.

The documentation is the archive compiled into the application: nothing is stubbed to read it, and the run speaks English, so the titles waited for are the English ones of the site (Help center, Installation, Install Apollia Desktop on macOS, Install Apollia Desktop on Windows, Architecture). A page renamed on the site moves these waits; the category ids are places in the sidebar tree (developer-docs-category-1 is the help center, -1-0 its Installation category, -6 the architecture), so a category added before them moves the ids.

plugin:opener|open_url resolves null so View on the web and the button under a diagram never reach the host browser; the address handed over is held by the Vitest suite. Copy as Markdown is clicked, not asserted, for the reason the address copy is. The fallback mention is played through a patch of get_documentation_page (DocsPage of crates/apollia-desktop/src/embedded_docs.rs, field fallback), since an English run never falls back; the unreadable page through a reject of the same command. Both are armed once and cleared before the documentation is left.
The book leaves the server stopped and the developer mode off, as it found them.
Not folded into master-det: this book has not been through a runtime round yet. Add it to ORDER in tools/regen_master.py after its first green solo run.

The server settings are opened with the server stopped, so switching CORS writes [server] cors in the apollia.toml of the seeded home and reopens nothing; it is switched back before the panel closes. The panel is a popover: the click that opened it closes it.

Code-verified against routes/Developer.svelte, components/developer/DeveloperColumn.svelte, ServerBar.svelte, LoadModelButton.svelte, LocalServerPane.svelte, DocumentationPane.svelte, LogsPane.svelte, LogLines.svelte and components/developer/localServer.ts and serverLogs.ts.

The logs are read from the real stream of the runtime of the seeded home, at the level chosen, and cleared through the real route. Their lines are not counted: what the server recorded by then depends on the run, and the lines themselves are held by the Vitest suite.

Detaching is stubbed on both sides: open_server_logs_window resolves as a window created without one being opened, since a second window would take the focus the capture relies on, and close_server_logs_window resolves false, the answer of crates/apollia-desktop/src/commands/logs_window.rs when no window is open, which brings the logs back to the screen. The real window is a manual gesture.

A stream that cannot be opened is stubbed: watch_server_logs rejects with a message, which shows the error and the offer to resume; the resume is then answered by a stub that opens no stream, so the empty state is certain whatever the server recorded. Both stubs are cleared before the last change of level, which reads the real stream again.

The rows of the server settings take their test ids from the names of the list of rows in components/developer/serverSettings.ts (developer-server-setting-<name>, with -control and -help for their parts), so they are declared dynamic here; a row renamed there drifts here silently.

The taken port of the settings and the server on the local network are stubbed: start_local_server and restart_local_server answer the LocalServerView or the LocalServerRefusal of crates/apollia-desktop/src/commands/local_server.rs, so no listener is opened on the network of the machine playing the book and [server] serve_on_lan is never written. What is written for real, and written back: port 7773 then 7772, require_auth on then off. A field renamed in that view drifts here silently.

The tokens are real: the book creates one token named Automation book in the system.db of the seeded home through the token routes of the runtime, reads the count of active tokens go to 1 in the settings, revokes it and reads the count come back to 0. The window is opened with the server stopped, so no listener is involved. The rows take their test ids from the identifiers the runtime gives (developer-server-token-row-<id>, with -revoke for the button), so the book clicks the last match of the prefix, which is the revoke button of the last row.

The unreadable list of tokens is stubbed once: list_server_tokens rejects with the text of an API error, the form the shell gives a failed GET. The copy of the token is clicked, not asserted, for the reason given for the address. The value of the token is never read into the report: the book only waits for its apo_ prefix, then for the value to be gone once the window was closed and opened again.

The id of a failure under the name of a token ends with the kind of the failure (developer-server-tokens-error-<kind>, components/developer/serverTokens.ts), so the one the book waits for is declared dynamic here.

The examples menu is opened on the first card, the stubbed model, with the server stopped: the examples are written for the address the state of the server reports, which a stopped server still has. Its entries and its copy buttons take their test ids from the list of examples in components/developer/examples.ts (developer-example-entry-<name>, developer-example-copy-<name>) and the choice of the SDK from its two names, so they are declared dynamic here. The copy buttons are clicked, not asserted, for the reason given for the address. The example with an MCP server provided by the request is reached by switching [server] allow_request_mcp on for real, in the apollia.toml of the seeded home, then off again; no request is ever sent.

The HTTP reference is read from the OpenAPI document compiled into the application: its category is the eighth of the tree (developer-docs-category-7, after the seven of the site), and the group of the tasks is named by its tag. A category added to the sidebar of the site, or the tag renamed in the contract, drifts here silently.
